A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we identify a new class of importance sampling distributions, which have the asymptotically efficient property for the estimation of density and large deviations of an average of IID light-tailed random variates.
we provide a simple recipe that allows one to efficiently estimate the density and probability of rare events.
for the estimation of density and the estimation of probability of large deviations, we have identified efficient importance sampling schemes, which are state dependent and asymptotically efficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, the asymptotically efficient importance sampling distribution is not the only distribution that can lead to asymptotically vanising relative error.
for a wide class of rare event estimation problems, the zero-variance distribution provides an efficient and robust estimator of the density and probability of rare events.

, for large deviations problems, the zero variance importance sampling measure can be efficiently approximated, and this leads to asymptotically efficient estimators for the density and the probability of a large deviation of a sum of independent random variables.
